saintsdragons.gui.draconic_codex.ecology: Raevyxians are ancient storm-bound apex predators whose dominance is expressed not through constant aggression, but through selective, overwhelming enforcement of territory. Emotionally aware and socially complex, they rely on inherited behaviors rather than instinct alone, making improper upbringing fatal. Their rarity is not due to weakness, but restraint.

Ignivoruses are primordial firebound titans whose presence reshapes environments through sheer thermal dominance. Unlike Raevyx, whose authority is enforced through restraint, Ignivoruses exert control by occupation. Where one settles, the land does not recover. Native primarily to the Nether, Ignivoruses are believed to have originated in extreme...

...volcanic ecosystems where constant exposure to magma and hellfire selected for organisms capable of converting ambient heat into sustained power. Their rare appearances in the Overworld are not migratory, but anomalous, often linked to ancient interdimensional traversal or forced displacement. Ignivoruses are not mindless engines of destruction. They are patient...
and acutely aware of hierarchy. Aggression is not constant, but once provoked, escalation is absolute. An Ignivorus does not retreat. It overwhelms.

Varasuchuses are adaptive abyssal predators whose threat lies not in overwhelming force, but in delayed commitment. Commonly encountered in coastal and aquatic regions, Varasuchus initially present as quadrupedal, semi-terrestrial hunters exhibiting restrained aggression and minimal energy expenditure. Early observers frequently misidentified this behavior...

...as docility or passivity. This assumption is universally fatal as Varasuchuses possess a unique phase-shifting physiology, allowing them to reconfigure posture, musculature, and combat behavior in response to sustained threat. The transition from quadrupedal to bipedal stance marks a decisive escalation, not an emotional one.

Once upright, Varasuchus abandon environmental tolerance and engage with deliberate, methodical violence. Their presence near civilization is rarely accidental. Records indicate that settlements which mistook Varasuchus’ initial restraint for safety rarely survived long enough to document its second phase.

Cindervanes are not conquerors, nor guardians. They are carriers. Early trade routes, evacuation corridors, and messenger networks were built around known Cindervane migratory paths. Their eggs, scattered rather than hoarded, suggest deliberate dispersion, either by the dragons themselves or by civilizations that understood...

...their value as mobile lifelines rather than weapons. Cindervanes lack complex combat instincts not due to weakness, but specialization. They do not linger in battle. When threatened, they escalate vertically, ignite, and end the encounter in a single decisive descent. Survival over supremacy.

Stegonauts' presence defines safe ground, forming mobile bastions around those they are bound to protect. Stegonauts exhibit strong social imprinting and defensive prioritization, willingly placing themselves between danger and allied entities without provocation. Historical accounts imply that early riders used Stegonauts as living shields during...

...dragon-mounted assaults, charging alongside faster aerial units while absorbing retaliatory force. This explains their compatibility with other mounts and their unique ability to protect allied pets and players mid-engagement.

Volitans dwell where land and water blur into one another. Where water stagnates long enough, where rot settles and refuses to leave, where fish float belly-up and the air carries a metallic sting… something begins to form beneath the surface. Not immediately. Not quickly. But inevitably. Unlike other dragons, Volitans do not chase prey across great distances...

They choose a territory… and become part of it. The water settles around them. The soil softens. The air itself carries a weight that lingers in the lungs. Intruders often mistake this for decay. It is not decay. It is pressure. Volitans do not rely on speed alone to dominate their domain. Instead, they reshape the battlefield. Toxic spines erupt not as...

...wild attacks, but as warnings… lines drawn in space. Their breath hangs in the air and clings to the ground, forcing movement, limiting escape. Despite their overwhelming presence, Volitans are not needlessly destructive. They do not scorch, nor do they ravage endlessly. Once intruders are driven out, the waters calm, the air clears, and the land returns to stillness.

Nulljaws are quiet End drifters that spend almost their entire existence suspended in open air. They neither dive for dominance nor settle into territory in the way other dragons do. Instead, they linger, observe, and glide in loose groups through the void-touched barrens.

dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.end_visit.res: Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.end_visit.end: Hm... aside from the Endermen and the Ender Dragon? I quite like it here.
As long as you don't look an Enderman in the eyes, you're fine. And after the Ender Dragon has been defeated, there's nothing to worry about.
I get to see the Nulljaws floating around, doing their own thing and minding their own business. I also get to try the 'local' cuisine, most notably Chorus Fruit.
I was teleported near the edge of the barrens when I bit into one! It would've been the end for me, pun intended, had a Nulljaw not saved me because it was attracted to the Chorus Fruit in my hand...
And I've always wondered what would hatch from the Ender Dragon's egg. I think it'd look like a slimmer Ignivorus, don't you?
But... there's one thing I've got to tell you.
Recently, travelers in the End have seen... horrid creatures. Not Nulljaws, of course, but dark, ravenous beasts whose birthing sacks have mysteriously appeared.
Thankfully, they only seem to spawn when approached.
However, their presence is quite concerning. I've only visited the End Barrens a few times, and I don't intend to venture there alone again.
With your help, however, we may be able to weaken them.
As we travel through the End Barrens, you'll see what I mean.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.first_meeting: Where was I? Ah, right.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
Oh, hi there. I didn't expect to see anyone here. Most people don't find this place by accident. You must love exploring, hm?
Maybe I'm not most people.
I'm sorry. Am I trespassing?
I was told a trader lived out here.
Who are you exactly?
Oh? That's either confidence or a warning. I haven't decided which. So... friendly or not?
I'm friendly.
I'm not friendly.
I was hoping you'd say that... it's nice to make your acquaintance.
Okaaay... Well, I was hoping you'd not say that...
ahem
No, you are not. Why would you think that? Oh, wait, yeah. It'd make sense for you to think so... but no, %1$s, you're not.
Welcome to my home. Where I live alone and... peaceful.
Ah, hey-ho, stranger. Yes. You found her. Would you like to see my wares?
Woah, what? Your 'wares' wares??
Yes, I'd like to trade with you.
...E-Excuse me? What--what was that supposed to mean? Was it such a good idea to say that to someone who you did not know?
Well, your fault for not specifying!
WHAT?? Wha--you should've... you shouldn't even be thinking about that in the first place!
Ugh...
Then? Would you like to trade with me?
See? That's so much better!
Yes, show me your wares.
Don't get smart...
Excellent. I have some good stuff you'd like to take a look at.
That's a fair question. A trader, mostly.
Gardener when the weather cooperates.
And occasionally the person people bother when they need dragon-related advice.
Though I suppose that doesn't really answer your question, does it?
It's a start.
With that being said, would you like to trade?
Yes, I'd like to trade with you.
No, I'm good.
I'll show you what I have.
Ah, I see. No worries.
Then we'll call it progress.
Well, anyway. My name is Ivy. Ivy Oleander. The last name is kind of uncommon. Rare, even. But yeah, you?
Tell her your name.
That's a pretty name.
Oleander? Isn't that poisonous?
Never heard that name before.
Just call me Ivy. Gonna tell me your name?
Tell her your name.
...Thank you. Most people just say it sounds like a plant. Which, well. It is. Two of them, actually.
Most people don't catch that. You're more observant than you look.
That's kind of the point, I think. My mother had a thing for unusual things.
Though if you've somehow met another Oleander, I'd be very interested to hear about it.
Anyway. What's your name?
Tell her your name.
What would you like me to call you?
Use your Minecraft username.
Choose what Ivy calls you.
What should I call you?
What am I calling you, then?
Use your Minecraft username.
Choose what Ivy calls you.
What should I call you?
It's a pleasure meeting you, %1$s. I'm sure we'll get along just fine.
Welp, not much of a pleasure, %1$s. But better than nothing.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.known_greetin: You again. Still not friendly, or was that just your opening act?
Well, if it isn't the 'not friendly' person.
Hi, 'friend.' Or maybe you're not friend?
Hello again. Still not trespassing, before you ask.
Oh it's the trespass-- %1$s, I mean, it's %2$s! Hi.
If you're here to make another joke, I reserve the right to charge extra.
What a great first impression you've just left behind...
Back again? I was starting to think the woods scared you off.
Ah, %1$s! I thought I heard something walking around.
Careful, %1$s. Keep showing up like this and I might think you enjoy my company.
Good to see you again! Try not to let that go to your head.
What do I do if you can't get to me?
What are your thoughts on the Nether, Ivy?
We're here in the End. What's on your mind?
What do you do out here?
You know a lot about dragons?
Oh, right! I'm glad you asked, actually. I almost forgot.
I'll give you an item that will help you, and it is quite important to me. I trust you'll keep it safe.
Whenever I can't get to you, use this, and well, something magical will happen, for lack of a better explanation.
I will be able to appear near you. I'll get used to being transported suddenly.
You're welcome. Try not lose it, hm? You won't get a second one.
Ah, I see you've made up your mind.
I'll stay here. Please don't die in your adventuring.
Please don't go for too long.
Don't you dare forget about me.
I'll be here eating dirt, then.
I'll be wandering around until you come back.
I'll hanging about until you come back.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.known_meeting: Where was I? Ah, right.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
You can say that, sure.
But it's enough to know when someone is about to get killed. Which is, unfortunately, often.
And it's enough to know people are usually wrong about them.
Wrong how?
Sounds complicated.
Most people talk about dragons like they're all the same. Big wings, sharp teeth, bad temper. Blah, blah, blah.
That's like saying every person with a sword is a knight.
Ahem
Or like, if a cat suddenly makes barking-like sounds, it's a dog. Does that make sense? No? %1$s, anyway.
Yep. I know. When it comes to dragons, it's not really a walk-in-the-park sort of situation.
I did have help from a guy with the name that has something to do with your diaphragm involuntarily slamming downward super fast.
And he had a really cute black dragon with him. Big green eyes. Almost like a cat. And it moved like one, too.
I've spent a lot of time studying dragons. Especially the Raevyx. But, uh, let's not talk about that.
Point is, dragons are more complicated than people want them to be.
Some are territorial. Some are curious. Some are clever enough to pretend they aren't.
And some... well. Some are best admired from a very safe distance and left alone.
So dragons aren't just monsters?
No, for most of the time.
But dangerous? Yes. Always.
But monster is a word people use when they don't want to understand what they're afraid of.
Volitans
Except for... the damn %1$s. Eugh. Steer clear from those weird freaks.
They are extremely lethal and sneaky despite their appearances. I almost got jumped by one when I was looking for a trident underwater...
And I was lucky enough to gather a lot of spines for arrows when they shed.
I could talk about dragons for hours, but that would be rude. Probably.
Anyway. That's probably more dragon talk than you asked for. I hope you weren't overwhelmed.

That rider you mentioned... who was he?
That's all for now.
Ah, right. A strange young chief. Clever. Awkward in a way that somehow worked for him.
I couldn't help but notice the prosthetic first time I met him.
I didn't ask too many questions. Some are better remembered as stories.
He had a black dragon with him. Big green eyes. Aerodynamic wings. Sleek body. Truly beautiful.
Moved like a cat. Looked at people like it knew exactly how stupid they were.
That dragon wasn't young. Not old either. But it carried itself like something that had survived more than a few bad ideas. I wish I had known its name.
But then the rider claimed his dragon was the fastest thing in the sky.
Which was rude, because my Raevyx was right there.
So we raced.
It was close. Almost a tie, actually.
Almost... I think he won. I don't know.
I would've liked to win, but... it was fun. Anyway, yeah, that's it. We exchanged goodbyes and that was that.
Where was I? Ah, right.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
A little trading, a little gardening, and a little making sure people don't do something ridiculous with dragons.
People do ridiculous things with dragons?
Gardening?
So you're a dragon expert?
That's all I need to know.
Anything else?
People do ridiculous things with dragons?
Gardening?
So you're a dragon expert?
That's all I need to know.
Oh, you have no idea. People, especially the villagers, have grown quite fond of some dragon species.
There was a villager I knew named Nimriel who was bucked off a juvenile Varasuchus while trying to ride it, and apparently, he broke his hip after hitting the ground.
And then someone fell off from a Cindervane, but luckily, they fell into a forest with dense trees.
Hah! Trees are still trees. Unlucky individual.
And then ME, specifically. Have you even heard of a Mossback?? Actually, here's a better one: why does that thing exist?!
I accidentally dropped one because it was slippery, and I got hit with a foul and overwhelming stench that blinded and POISONED me!
The audacity of those things. To have wings and cannot fly while being fat, and stinky?! Ugh...
I had to wait it out. I was sweating the whole time like a sinner in a church pew while I was at it...
After the effects had worn off, it ran away, the little prick... funny thing is, they don't even react when you pick them up. And you can throw them.
Don't even dare throw one at me, though. I'll hate you forever...
So yes. People do ridiculous things with dragons.
Sometimes the dragons do ridiculous things back.
Mhm. Gardening.
Plants are easier to negotiate with. Usually.
I grow herbs, roots, flowers, a few things that are useful for medicine...
...and a few things that are useful when medicine is no longer the plan.
Relax. I label the dangerous ones. Most of the time.
Well... not really. Expert is a dangerous word.
People hear it and start assuming you know everything. I don't.
Villagers often ask me how to tame certain types of dragons. I teach them the proper methods, make sure they're prepared, and send them off with enough knowledge and equipment to not die immediately.
A lot of the time, they still fail miserably.
Not because they're stupid. Well... not always.
Most just don't have the patience, caution, or nerve to deal with a wild dragon.
And then some ask me how to tame a Raevyx while looking like a tumbleweed with pockets.
Like, come on. You look like that and want to tame THE GRIM REAPER?! They can barely tame a Cindervane!
Ahem. Sorry. I didn't mean to yell.
Sometimes I think, 'Wouldn't it be easier to look for an egg and raise one from the start?'
But even that takes patience. And fish. An unreasonable amount of fish.
Anyway.
I know enough to stay humble. That's more than most experts can say.
The moment someone says they understand dragons completely, I start looking for the nearest exit.
Or a shovel.
Depends how confident they sound.
Gotcha.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
I can't even think because it's too hot...
I've gone into the Nether a few times to look for Netherite and smaller things like Glowstone Dust and Nether Wart... but I failed on the Netherite part.
Simply because I can't stand the heat or some of the denizens here.
I kind of like the biomes, especially the Crimson Forest. It reminds me of the color of my dragon...
Also, I absolutely hate the Piglins. I almost got jumped because I forgot to wear my gold helmet.
Don't get me started on the Ghasts. Why do they make those weird sounds? How can they float? Why do they look so creepy? I didn't do anything to them, and I still got a fireball shot at me?!
Striders are just weird old men with toothpicks for legs, standing in a lake of lava.
I tried luring one onto land and dragging it back to the Overworld, but seeing it shiver out of the lava made me pity it.
And Wither Skeletons and Blazes? Absolutely not. Bunch of freaks...
The point is, the Nether is weird, which circles back to it having its own charm, I think. And I only came along because you're with me. Otherwise, I'd never look twice at it.
I'm sweating a lot right now... Let's just hurry up with whatever you're trying to do and get out of this place, please?
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.quest_cinderv: Yes? Have you encountered any trouble?
Can you go over it one more time?
I haven't done it yet.
I did it. I've tamed a Cindervane.
Of course. It's better to ask twice than rush in unsure.
...Something the matter? It's alright. Take your time.
You can do it. I'll be rooting for you.
Now go and get your first dragon.
You did? And you came back with all your limbs intact and not dead?
That's already better than most!
How did it go?
I followed your advice.
It wasn't that hard.
It tried to burn me a little.
That's good! I do take pride in my advice sometimes.
Especially when dragons are involved.
Ah-ah. Careful now.
Dragons hear arrogance better than commands. But I suppose you are right. Cindervanes are quite straightforward to deal with.
But... regardless, you did succeed. So, good job.
...Didn't I tell you not to hit it?
Well, I'm still glad you didn't die. Good job.
Most people want dragons to obey. You let one choose. And that matters a lot to me. More than people think.
So, did I prove myself?
What now?
You sound surprised.
Hah! Get a load of this... You're humble. I like it.
Come on, that Cindervane is child's play for someone like you.
A little. But don't let it inflate your head, ok?
You haven't seen what others can do. But if you had, then well, I hereby take everything back.
But yes. You handled that well.
Mm... now? Maybe having a companion like you wouldn't be a bad idea at all.
Now? Now I decide whether following you is brave, useful, or a terrible lapse in judgment. But it's possibly all three.
Well, I'm not, actually. I already know you can handle yourself pretty well.
I am. Not because I thought you'd fail. But because I've seen plenty of confident people fail loudly.
I've been thinking... staying here has its comforts, you know?
Quiet mornings. Familiar paths. Fewer things trying to bite me. No Mossbacks...
But problems involving dragons rarely come knocking politely at my door.
If I travel with you, maybe I can stop a few before they become tragedies. And... sightsee more. And dragonwatching. And... I'm gonna stop myself from rambling.
Come with me, then.
Only if you want to.
I could use your help.
Are you sure? Very well. Here to a bountiful future.
I don't want to. What are you gonna do about it?
Pfft--
%1$s I was just kidding! You should've seen the look on your face...
Well... I didn't say that. But yes. I want to.
Yes. And I could use yours.
I'll come with you.
Just promise me one thing.
What?
Treat your dragons well.
Let's get going, %1$s.
Cindervanes are migrating this season, and that tends to make people reckless.
I want you to tame one. Properly, that is. Just to test your mettle.
How do I tame a Cindervane?
No way. I'm out.
I suggest you look for food items like cod, salmon, or raw chicken. Or everything. They are not picky when hungry.
If you want better odds, trade with me for fish and eggs. I can make you Hearty Dragon Meals.
Once you have the food, look for Cindervanes in mountainous biomes, like Stony Peaks, Jagged Peaks, Frozen Peaks, Snowy Slopes, Groves, and even Meadows.
...And potentially other high-altitude areas from other 'biome mods' or whatever that means.
Once you've found one, just approach it, and tame it like how you would tame a dog or a cat.
Do NOT hit it. Please. If you've somehow made it mad, then it's best to run away, or chug a Fire Resistance Potion, or worse... kill it.
When you've tamed one, come back to me, then we'll see where things go.
Is everything clear?
Can you go over it one more time?
Crystal clear.
I already tamed a Cindervane.
You... You already tamed one?
Well... That certainly makes this easier! I suppose I do not need to explain the dangerous part anymore.
Very well. I'll explain again. It's good to be thorough.
Good. Come back once you've tamed one.
...Very well. I understand why you are hesitant.
And honestly, that's one of the more reasonable answers I've heard.
We'll revisit the matter later, if you want to, of course.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_gre: Glad to have you with me.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_vis: I already have a travelling companion. But I can still trade with you.
I am spoken for, in the companion sense. The shop is still open, though.
Sorry. My companion and I travel together. That does not mean I have stopped being a trader.
There's little I can say to you, I'm afraid. We can still trade.
Sorry. There's only so much of me to go around. We can still trade.
You seem nice and all, but I've teamed up with someone else. We can still trade, though.
Hello to you too. Take care.
